title:
Pursue, Overtake,
Recover All
paragraphs: Ziklag wasn't a rumor David heard about — he walked into the smoke himself. Everything that mattered was gone: the homes, the supplies, his own wives, and six hundred men who'd just watched their families get carried off too. Scripture doesn't hide the moment it almost came apart — his own soldiers, grieving and furious, started talking about stoning the man they'd followed into every other battle. That's the scene most people quit in: devastated, surrounded, and suddenly alone even in a crowd of six hundred.

But David didn't call a meeting. He didn't defend his record or argue with the grief talking out loud around him. He went to God first — encouraged himself in the Lord, then asked the only question that mattered: shall I pursue? Heaven didn't just say yes. It said pursue, for thou shalt surely overtake them, and without fail recover all. Whatever Ziklag burned down in your life, the same God who sent David after his family is still in the business of 'without fail' — not almost, not partially, all.
